prompt: Solve the inequality $-4x + 3 < 23$. Write your answer like "x > -5".
hint: Get the $x$ term alone first, then decide what dividing by its coefficient does to the sign.

hints.text: Get the $x$ term alone first, then decide what dividing by its coefficient does to the sign.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Simpler: $-4x < 8$ gives $x > -2$ (sign flips!). Yours just needs the $+3$ moved over first.
Subtract $3$ from both sides to get $-4x < 20$. Then divide by $-4$ and reverse the sign, so $<$ becomes $>$.
$20 \div (-4) = -5$ and the sign flips, so the solution set is $x > -5$.

explanation: Subtract $3$ from both sides, which leaves the sign alone: $-4x < 20$.
Divide both sides by $-4$ and flip $<$ to $>$, because dividing by a negative reverses the order: $x > -5$.
Check: $x = 0$ gives $3 < 23$, which is true, while $x = -6$ gives $24 + 3 = 27$, which fails. So the answer is $x > -5$.

alternativeExplanations.title: On a number line
steps: Put an OPEN dot at $-5$, since $-5$ itself gives $23 < 23$, which is false.
Shade to the right: every number bigger than $-5$ makes the left side smaller than 23.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ Dodge the trap
steps: x < −5 keeps the sign pointing the old way after dividing by −4 — the classic missing flip.
Check with x = 0: −4(0) + 3 = 3 < 23 ✓, so 0 must be in the answer. Only x > −5 contains 0.
